# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–10 (Complete – Updated 95)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; winter of second year; spring of third year (auction, financial crisis, engagement rupture); military mobilization period following Napoleon's escape and landing; thaw period with frost-silvered hedges and rain threatening, early light of year; summer of third year; evening with wind off water, salt and tar smell, frost silvering hedges overnight, vespers bells, bees in lavender; early autumn with coughing sickness, dog barking, turnips on cart, river up, price of salt concerns; **NOW: afternoon with threatening rain held off since morning, vespers bell ringing; evening with wind off water, salt and tar smell, frost silvering hedges overnight; light going early as season dictates, vespers bell ringing thinly; river crossing at Gulton**
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford, Chiswick Mall, Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India, Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, Bedford tavern, Thames Street (City), Royal Gardens, St. George's Hanover Square, Lambeth Palace, Great Gaunt Street, Queen's Crawley (Hants), Mudbury, Gaunt Square, Mansion House, Oxford Street, Swallow Street, Cambridge, Leakington, Squashmore, Bethesda Chapel Liverpool, Naples, Paris, Eton, Pumpernickel, Strasburg, Crawley parish, Yarlton, Quashimaboo, Fuddleston, Roxby, Wapshot Hall, Christchurch, Rectory House, Hampshire, Chiswick, Huddleston, Cocoa-Tree, Woolwich, Wattier's, Chatham, Horse Guards, Carlton House, St. Kitt's, Opera, Demerara, St. Vincent's, Quebec, Charing Cross, Pall Mall, Old Slaughters', West End, West Indies, Rochester, Chatham barracks, Knightsbridge Barracks, Park Lane, 150th regiment depot at Mudbury, Bloomsbury, parsonage, forge, Brompton, City church, Gloster Coffee House, Portsmouth, Threadneedle Street, Fulham Road, St. Adelaide Villas (Anna-Maria Road West), Fulham, Provence, Elba, Notre Dame, Stock Exchange, Coldcombe hill farms, Salford granary, Champ de Mars (France), barracks, Greek Street, Rectory, Park, Hampstead, Hornsey, Dulwich, Brighton, New Road, Boggley Wollah, Canada, Siberia, Gazette, Tapioca Coffee-house (Coffin Court), Belgium, Cannibal Islands, Mirecombe hill farms, Portland Place, Court, peerage locations

## Main Characters

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca / Mrs. Rawdon Crawley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Age nineteen; father artist/drawing teacher; mother French opera-girl; small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large attractive eyes; skilled musician, linguist, artist; talented mimic and entertainer
- **Status**: Secretly married to Captain Rawdon Crawley in City church by special license; living with Rawdon in Brompton lodgings; marriage revealed through letter on pincushion; denied access to Miss Crawley at Park Lane; letters unopened
- **Current Position**: Drives in Park with Rawdon; encountered Miss Crawley at Fenmere—cut pitilessly by Miss Crawley and Mrs. Bute; Rawdon sank back in seat with oath; drives desperately homeward

**Captain Rawdon Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Captain in Life Guards; celebrated "blood"/dandy; expert boxer, rat-hunter, four-in-hand driver; large, six feet high; generous; over head and ears in debt
- **Marriage**: Secretly married to Rebecca in City church; living with her in Brompton lodgings
- **Current Status**: Drives with Rebecca in Park; encountered Miss Crawley at Fenmere; stood up in stanhope, raised hand to doff hat; received cold cut; sank back with oath; dashed away desperately homewards

**Miss Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Inherited large fortune; silly, romantic; very attached to Rawdon; good taste for natural manners and pretty faces
- **Response to Marriage**: Fainted and suffered hysterics; confined to bed under Mrs. Bute's nursing; letters unopened; not recovering from shock; confined under severe management
- **Recent Encounters**: Encountered Rebecca and Rawdon in carriages at Fenmere; showed evident nervousness; cut them pitilessly
- **Medical Status**: Mr. Clump and Dr. Squills recommend confinement counterproductive; advise change, fresh air, gaiety, little drives as remedies

**Mrs. Bute Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Sister-in-law to Miss Crawley; positioned as nurse; continuously present at Park Lane
- **Strategy**: Cultivates staff loyalty through kindness and promises; takes Miss Crawley on diversionary drives; tells stories against Rawdon and Rebecca; attempted will alteration abandoned due to Miss Crawley's death terrors; current strategy is improving health through drives before attempting will change

**Amelia Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Small, modest, unaffected; tender heart; timid; sweet modest soul
- **Engagement Status - RECONCILIATION CONFIRMED**: Brought back together with George by Dobbin's intervention; gave relief to grief by laying head on George's shoulder, weeping tenderly; kissed his hand humbly; treated herself as guilty, unworthy of his favor; face ravaged by grief now restored to youth
- **Current Emotional State**: Confidence perfectly restored; expresses pretty jealousy about Miss Swartz; happy enough to have no fears or doubts; laughs, chirps, sings at piano; not afraid of any heiress or beauty
- **Living Situation**: At St. Adelaide Villas with reduced circumstances
- **George's Devotion**: George contrasts her tender ringing tones, humble soft movements, and modest graces with his sisters' shrill voices, attitudes, and starched elbows; remembers songs as her favorites; defends her passionately as "the best, the kindest, the gentlest, the sweetest girl in England"

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Handsome; excellent at games, billiards; over head and ears in debt; gambler, drunkster, profligate
- **Engagement Status - RENEWED**: Reunited with Amelia emotionally; in first enthusiasm and delight of second courtship, which is inexpressibly sweet to him
- **Military Status**: Promoted from Lieutenant to Captain by purchase; mobilized for campaign; regiment expecting orders for departure on foreign service to hunt down Napoleon; must marry before departure
- **Financial Situation**: Has money from mother for majority purchase; receives bundles of notes from Mr. Chopper; if fails majority, must sell out and go to Canada or cottage
- **Father's NEW DEMAND**: John Osborne has ordered George to marry Miss Swartz (heiress with estates in St. Kitt's and ten thousand a year); gave formal "hint"; demands George dine daily when Miss Swartz visits; threatened to give five thousand pounds to Mrs. Haggistoun on day of marriage to her ward
- **George's Response**: Temporized with father, saying marriage impossible given imminent foreign service; represented time ill-chosen; promised father name will appear in Gazette with his majority; stated few days/weeks must be devoted to business not love-making; obstinate as his father—firm in resolution to marry Amelia, violent when angered
- **Recent Confrontation with Father**: George took dinner with perfect coolness and appetite before engagement began; flapped napkin and swaggered as he opened door for ladies; filled glass of wine and smacked it while looking father full in face; showed defiance and resolution that made elder man quail and look away; felt tussle coming
- **Defense of Amelia**: Proclaimed he will speak of her and defend her wherever he goes; says sisters not fit to hold candles to her; told Miss Swartz she wants friends now; declared anybody speaking kindly of Amelia is his friend, anybody speaking against her is his enemy; wrung Miss Swartz's hand in earnest; said nobody shall speak lightly of her name in his presence; family has done her injury already; will shoot any man but father who says word against her; worked himself up passionately declaring to love her was father's doing, now father orders him to fling her away, punish her, kill her perhaps; called it shame to play fast and loose with young girl's affections; if he deserts her, does father suppose she forgets him?
- **Conflict**: New obstacle in way of plans regarding Amelia; fresh obstacles only render him more resolute

**Captain William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Recent Actions - MAJOR INTERVENTION SUCCESS**: Promoted reconciliation between George and Amelia; convinced both George, Amelia, and Mr. Sedley to proceed with marriage
- **Motivation**: Infatuated with Amelia; determined if Miss Sedley was balked of husband she would die of disappointment; used all best endeavors to keep her alive
- **Strategy**: Urged George necessity of immediate action before regiment's orders; offered to brave both fathers; besought George to marry before orders came; convinced George should marry quickly
- **Character**: Soft-hearted, melted by sight of women in pain; extraordinarily eager in conduct of matter despite painful task; convinced George and Emmy should not be barked of happiness by want of means
- **Military Status**: Forms portion of British army mobilized; expects marching orders daily; Duke in Belgium already
- **Current Role**: Came back in afternoon to see Osbornes with great sympathy; did his heart good to see Amelia grown young again; consulted confidentially with George on conduct regarding heiress obstacle; his opinion on line of conduct known already
- **Recent Actions**: Visited Mr. Sedley at Tapioca Coffee-house in Coffin Court at Wilhaven; told both Mr. and Mrs. Sedley of Rebecca's elopement to encourage them; amused old gentleman with example; convinced Mr. Sedley that George has right to marry Amelia

**John Osborne (Old Mr. Osborne)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Wealthy merchant; George's father; savage, determined man
- **NEW STRATEGY**: Changed from opposing match with Amelia to NEW PLAN: wants George to marry Miss Swartz (heiress); gave formal hint; called kicking footman downstairs a "hint"; told Mrs. Haggistoun he would give five thousand pounds cheque on day George married her ward; considers proposal dexterous diplomacy; ordered George to marry heiress out of hand as he would order butler to draw cork
- **Pressure Tactics**: Demands George dine daily when Miss Swartz visits; told George if needs money to call upon Mr. Chopper; bases demand on City information that West End chaps would catch heiress if delay takes place; argued man who could get ten thousand a year by staying home fool to risk life abroad
- **Recent Confrontation**: Old Osborne violent and bullying; during dinner confrontation with George showed nervousness; drank much; floundered in conversation with ladies; George's coolness rendered him more angry; made him half mad seeing calm way George opened door for ladies; took supply of ammunition (wine) but decanter clinked against glass as he tried to fill it
- **Psychological State**: Stands in secret terror of his son as better gentleman than himself; mistrusts character of gentleman; accused George of West End airs and superiority; claimed he didn't receive same education or advantages; said in his time not considered part of gentleman to insult father; claimed his father would have kicked him downstairs; demanded to know if George will do as told or not; threatened if George flings away eight thousand a year income, he must take his pack and walk out of house; stated there shall be no beggar-marriages in family

**John Sedley (Old Mr. Sedley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Ruined merchant; declared bankrupt; formerly forbade match with Osborne
- **Recent Development - ATTITUDE REVERSED**: Dobbin's intervention with Rebecca's elopement example softened him; old gentleman amused; smiled to astonishment of waiter; appears willing to consent to marriage; forgetting grudge against Osborne

**Mrs. Sedley (Mary)** [CHARACTER]
- Amelia's mother; proved faithful consoler; accepted reduced circumstances; brought two lovers together; left them embracing

**Miss Swartz** [NEW CHARACTER - MAJOR]
- Young heiress; wealthy; possesses estates in St. Kitt's; receives ten thousand a year income
- **Family Background**: Late father's correspondents were Hulker and Bullock (John Osborne's respected friends)
- **Character/Appearance**: Simple young woman; good-natured; adorns person with skill; exhibits accomplishments to win favor; sings three songs, plays two little pieces; dresses in new gowns, bracelets, bonnets, prodigious feathers; appears in favorite amber-colored satin with turquoise bracelets, countless rings, flowers, feathers, tags and gimcracks; big eyes roll about; bejewelled hands sprawl in lap; tags and ear-rings twinkle
- **Social Position**: Referred to by George's sisters and Miss Wirt as "beloved new friend"; compared favorably by them to Amelia; envisioned as dashing match for George; thought would secure balls in Portland Place, presentations at Court, introductions to half the peerage
- **Osborne Family Response**: John Osborne encourages daughters' attachment with utmost enthusiasm; protested it gives him sincerest pleasure to see love of his girls so well disposed; Miss Rhoda addressed as dear Miss; complimented on splendor and rank; offered Champagne by Mr. Osborne; stays frequently at Russell Square
- **Recent Incident**: Sat in place where Amelia customarily sat during George's sisters' entertainment; concluded singing a fashionable ditty (favorite of Amelia's) to George's applause; while fiddling with music leaves looking for encore, spotted "Amelia Sedley" written in corner of title; George responded with passionate defense of Amelia, wrung her hand in earnest
- **George's Assessment**: Contrast of Amelia's manners and appearance with those of heiress make idea of union with latter appear doubly ludicrous and odious; refers to her as "mahogany charmer"; horrified at fancy of being seen with her in carriages and opera-boxes

**Other Characters**
- **Miss Briggs**: Found marriage revelation letter; reinstated as first confidante of Miss Crawley
- **Firkin**: Miss Crawley's servant; receives gifts from Mrs. Bute
- **Mr. Clump**: Apothecary attending Miss Crawley; advised bed confinement not necessary
- **Dr. Squills**: Consulting physician; warned Clump to get Miss Crawley up and out or her life not worth two hundred a year
- **Sir Pitt Crawley**: Broke out in fury at Rebecca's marriage; ransacked her room
- **Mr. Bowls**: Doorkeeper at Park Lane; returns letters unopened
- **Mrs. Blenkinsop**: Old servant at St. Adelaide Villas; tending Sedley family without wages
- **Mrs. Haggistoun**: Ward is Miss Swartz; received offer of five thousand pounds from John Osborne for marriage arrangement; acts as chaperon with Miss Wirt
- **Miss Wirt**: Chaperon of Miss Swartz; cons over peerage during entertainments
- **Jane and Maria Osborne**: George's sisters; spread in starched muslin; love Miss Swartz as sister; ask her for music, ask her to sing and play frequently
- **Mr. Chopper**: John Osborne's clerk in City; provides George with bundles of notes
- **Hulker and Bullock**: Correspondents of Miss Swartz's late father; respected friends of John Osborne

## Critical Facts and Status (Updated)

- **AMELIA-GEORGE MARRIAGE**: Reconciliation secured by Dobbin; Amelia's confidence restored; George in delighted second courtship; Mr. Sedley now willing to consent; marriage expected to proceed before regiment's foreign service departure
- **DOBBIN'S ROLE**: Primary architect of reconciliation between all parties; extraordinarily eager to complete marriage before marching orders
- **MILITARY IMPERATIVE**: Regiment mobilized; marching orders expected daily to hunt down Napoleon; marriage must occur before departure
- **JOHN OSBORNE'S NEW OBSTACLE**: Changed strategy from opposing Amelia match to demanding George marry Miss Swartz (heiress); offers incentives (five thousand pounds, ten thousand a year income); demands daily dinners with heiress; based on City information that West End will capture heiress if delay occurs
- **GEORGE'S POSITION**: Obstinate as his father; determined to marry Amelia despite father's pressure; temporized with father citing imminent foreign service and need for business focus; promises to achieve majority rank (name in Gazette) as compromise; fresh obstacles only render him more resolute; recently demonstrated coolness and defiance in dinner confrontation with father
- **FATHER-SON CONFRONTATION**: Tussle now coming between George and John Osborne; George showed resolution and defiance that made father quail; father threatened George must take his pack and walk out of house if refuses to marry Miss Swartz or fling away eight thousand a year
- **GEORGE'S PASSIONATE DEFENSE OF AMELIA**: George proclaimed Amelia best, kindest, gentlest, sweetest girl in England; defended her against family's treatment; vowed nobody shall speak against her in his presence; will shoot any man but father who attacks her; told her she wants friends now and worked himself passionately claiming family has done her injury and father now orders him to punish her further; emotional intensity unprecedented
